data.funding: Binance Vision futures/um monthly fundingRate archives for the 30 crypto pairs, 2022-01..2026-10; every zip SHA-256 verified against its published .CHECKSUM before use; canonical per-symbol CSV + sidecar manifest (csv_sha256, per-month zip hashes, absent months) in the crew cache; the runner re-verifies each CSV's hash at load
data.ohlcv: RD-002 Stage-A caches (128 hash-manifested series), reused unchanged via rd2.panels
data.uncovered: overnight_drift on indices: Yahoo cash-index 1h bars exist only 13:00-21:00 UTC (RTH), so the overnight window does not exist in the data — mechanism UNCOVERED on idx panels, not approximated

declaration_rule: This declaration, the family code (rd3/families_rd3.py) and the runner (rd3/run_families.py) ship in a dedicated PR merged BEFORE the first Stage-2 cell is executed. No variant, threshold, cell or exit spec below may be altered after that merge; any change would be a new declaration and new trials.

families.differentiation: No RD-001/RD-002 family used funding data or any non-OHLCV series; the signal source itself is new to the programme.
families.mechanism: Perpetual funding prints are a direct positioning/crowding gauge invisible to OHLCV. FADE claim: when the last print sits in the extreme tail of its own trailing 540-print distribution AND price is extended in the funding direction (vs EMA50), the crowded side is fadeable. CARRY claim: when the print is large, take the side that receives funding. Judgement is PRICE-ONLY (funding cashflows are not added to trade returns, by declared harness convention — conservative for the carry claim).
families.name: funding_extremes

signal_rules.carry: SHORT if last print > thr; LONG if last print < -thr
signal_rules.fade: SHORT if pct >= pctl and close > EMA50(close); LONG if pct <= 1-pctl and close < EMA50
signal_rules.features: per bar open T: last print at or before T; mean3 = mean of last 3 prints; pct = percentile rank of the last print within the trailing 540 prints (min 60); gates: >= 160 days of print history before T, last print age <= 24h

families.differentiation: RD-002's session_effects were crypto 1h intraday momentum/reversal patterns and batch-3's session_breakout trades range breakouts at London/NY opens; neither holds the overnight window itself nor trades its sign dynamics, and neither ran outside crypto.
families.mechanism: Session return decomposition outside crypto: the 21:00->07:00 UTC window (New York close to Europe open) is a distinct return regime. DRIFT claim: holding that window outright earns a premium. FADE claim: the window mean-reverts against its own previous completed window.
families.name: overnight_drift

signal_rules.exit: bracket_time sl 3.0 / tp 6.0 ATR, max_bars 11 (time exit at the 07:00 bar's close dominates by construction)
signal_rules.fade: opposite side of the previous completed window's return (close of 07:00 bar / open of 21:00 bar - 1)
signal_rules.signal_bar: the 20:00 UTC bar (fill at the 21:00 open)

families.differentiation: All judged crypto families are single-asset (own-series signals) or cross-sectional rank-based (xs_momentum/xs_reversal); none conditions one asset's trades on another asset's move.
families.mechanism: Cross-asset information diffusion: BTC is the crypto complex's information leader; a large BTC trailing move predicts alt returns over the following k bars as the move propagates. BTC itself is never traded (trading BTC on its own move would be ts_momentum, already judged).
families.name: btc_leadlag

signal_rules.exit: bracket_time sl 2.0 / tp 4.0 ATR, max_bars = k
signal_rules.signal: for each alt bar: BTC ROC(k) vs theta x BTC ATR%(14), both mapped onto the alt's bars by asof (tolerance 65 min); LONG if ROC > theta*ATR%, SHORT if ROC < -theta*ATR%

families.differentiation: Components (donchian breakout, z-score reversion) were judged standalone in RD-002, and vol_adaptive_trend gates ONE trend strategy by a vol percentile; no judged configuration selects between opposing strategy classes by regime. Disclosed simplification: the two sleeves are simulated independently (one-position rule applies per sleeve, not across), and their trades are pooled — the same accounting spirit as RD-002 Stage C's sleeve construction.
families.mechanism: Volatility-regime-conditional strategy-class selection: breakout continuation is traded only in low-volatility regimes (ATR% trailing-200 percentile rank <= lo), z-score reversion only in high regimes (rank >= hi), flat between. The claim under test is the SWITCH, not either component.
families.name: vol_regime_switch

signal_rules.breakout_sleeve: donchian-20 breakout entries on bars with rank <= lo; exit bracket sl 2.0 / tp 4.0 ATR
signal_rules.regime: rank = ATR%(14) trailing-200 percentile rank (pandas rolling rank, pct)
signal_rules.reversion_sleeve: z-score(20, 2.0) crossing entries on bars with rank >= hi; exit bracket sl 2.0 / tp 2.0 ATR

judgement.bar: expectancy_net > 0 AND profit_factor_net >= 1.2 AND >= 200 OOS trades AND >= 80% of fold-profile folds positive AND holdout2 pass (breadth >= 50% of active symbols positive, max symbol profit share <= 50% on panels >= 5 symbols, untouched every-3rd-symbol subset positive on >= 30 trades)
judgement.costs: per rd2/costs2.py, unchanged from RD-002 (crypto 16 bps RT; forex majors 6 / minors 10; GOLD 10, SILVER 14, WTI 12, BRENT 12, NATGAS 20, COPPER 12, PLATINUM 14; indices 8)
judgement.counting: one (config, panel, timeframe) cell = one trial; one wf-select procedure per (family, panel, timeframe) with >= 2 variants = one trial; the global counter continues from RD-002's final 1,557
judgement.folds: STANDARD W1-W5 except Yahoo-1h-derived intraday panels (LATE W2-W5), per rd2.panels.fold_profile
judgement.sensitivity: every mechanical-bar passer is re-run at 2x costs and must keep PF >= 1.2
judgement.significance: Bonferroni one-sided p < 0.05 / N_final, computed at RD-003's FINAL global trial count (gate, per RD-002's stated method); deflated Sharpe computed and disclosed for every near-bar row, not gating
